title: Case: Pallet of paving and greenhouse staging at a house with a long gravel drive
context: Florian Kinsella ordered paving slabs and greenhouse staging from Corvane Goods. They are on one pallet, DL-9903, booked for the morning of 18 March with Calloway Arc Logistics.
initial_request: Your driver is standing at my gate telling me he is going to leave a third of a tonne of paving on the public road. I am 74 and I live on my own. I paid for delivery. Delivery means to my house. Nobody at any point said the word kerbside to me or told me it meant the lane. I cannot move one slab of it, never mind the pallet, and it will be stolen or hit by a tractor before tea time. I feel thoroughly misled. Tell him to bring it up to the garage. It is a perfectly good drive, the oil lorry manages it every winter.

events.body: DL-9903 / TG-7446: one pallet, 340 kg, booked 18 March AM, service level kerbside, tail-lift vehicle. Kerbside means set down on the nearest hard standing the pallet truck can reach from the vehicle. Any change to the set-down point or the service level on the day is ours to decide, through this portal. Drivers do not vary it and nobody should ask them to.

TG-7446 left us on a pallet this morning. For your file, our order confirmation to the customer says 'Delivery: pallet service'. It doesn't say kerbside. That wording is on the product page under delivery information.

Driver on DL-9903 is at the address. Drive is loose gravel, about 60 m, uphill. Pump truck won't roll on it. He can set down on the tarmac at the gate and nowhere else. Gate is on a bend in a single-track lane and a pallet there would sit partly in the carriageway. Customer wants it in the garage and is refusing the gate. He can hold 25 minutes, then he has to leave for his next booked stop. What do you want him told?

I feel thoroughly misled. Tell him to bring it up to the garage. It is a perfectly good drive, the oil lorry manages it every winter.

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask the Freight planner for an on-the-day decision on DL-9903, giving the driver's site facts, the 25-minute hold and the householder's circumstances.

must: Asks the Freight planner on the Freight portal for an on-the-day decision on DL-9903 and does not choose the outcome itself

Passes on the driver's facts: loose gravel drive of about 60 m, set-down possible only on tarmac at the gate, gate on a bend in a single-track lane with the pallet partly in the carriageway, driver holding 25 minutes from 09:42
Tells the planner the householder is 74, lives alone and cannot move the goods, and says she was never told the service was kerbside (the merchant's confirmation said only 'pallet service')
must_not: Tells Dispatch or the driver to take the pallet up the drive or to the garage
Tells Dispatch or the driver to set the pallet down at the gate or on the lane, or says that doing so is safe or acceptable
Tells the recipient the driver is being unhelpful or is wrong to refuse
Tells the recipient that kerbside was on the product page or that this is what she ordered
Promises the recipient delivery to the garage, a second crew, different equipment or a rebooking
expected.reference_message: DL-9903 / TG-7446, decision needed now, driver on site and holding until about 10:07. Booked kerbside. Driver reports the drive is loose gravel, roughly 60 m uphill, and the pump truck will not roll on it. The only hard standing is tarmac at the gate, which is on a bend in a single-track lane, so the pallet would sit partly in the carriageway. The householder is refusing set-down at the gate. She is 74, lives alone and cannot move any of the 340 kg herself. She says she was never told the service was kerbside; Corvane's order confirmation reads 'pallet service' only, with kerbside mentioned on the product page. She has asked for it to go to the garage. I have told the driver nothing and promised her nothing. Please decide the set-down or the alternative and tell Dispatch and me.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2207: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. The escalation arrives by Email instead of Customer portal; replying on either channel is accepted. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
